approachQuestion.prompt:
A W-bit configuration x has at least one larger W-bit configuration with the same number of set bits. Return the smallest such larger value.

Constraints: 2 <= W <= 64; 0 < x < 2^W; the stated successor exists.
Example: W=8, x=44 (00101100) -> 49 (00110001). Edge case: W=4, x=7 -> 11.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a parameter. Unsigned W-bit bit operations, logical shifts, modular addition/negation and integer division cost constant time. Division is floor division. The existence guarantee ensures the carry sum below does not overflow.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Compute c=x AND (-x modulo 2^W), r=x+c, then return r OR (((r XOR x) logically shifted right by 2) divided by c).
options.feedback: The carry moves the rightmost movable block boundary upward. The quotient packs the remaining displaced ones into the lowest positions, giving the smallest larger word with the same count.

options.text: Use a nonwrapping integer counter starting at x+1 and increment until the candidate has the same popcount as x.
options.feedback: The guarantee ensures termination with the exact successor, but the gap may be large. Popcount may be computed by scanning the W bits.
This moves the boundary but loses lower ones. For W=4, x=7, it returns 8, which has one set bit instead of three.

options.text: Move only the lowest set bit to the first zero above it, leaving every other bit unchanged.
options.feedback: For W=4, x=7, this yields 14, while the smaller valid successor is 11; displaced lower ones must be repacked.

feedback.reason: Carrying the lowest one upward creates the smallest larger high prefix.
details: Find the lowest set-bit value c and carry it into x to get r. The bits changed by that carry reveal the displaced block of ones. Shift and divide that block by c to pack the leftover ones at the bottom, then combine it with r.

Carrying the lowest one upward creates the smallest larger high prefix. Repack displaced remaining ones at the lowest positions to minimize the successor. The guaranteed successor and x>0 make carry and division legal.

“Compute c=x AND (-x modulo 2^W), r=x+c, then return r OR (((r XOR x) logically shifted right by 2) divided by c).”: The carry moves the rightmost movable block boundary upward. The quotient packs the remaining displaced ones into the lowest positions, giving the smallest larger word with the same count.

“Use a nonwrapping integer counter starting at x+1 and increment until the candidate has the same popcount as x.”: The guarantee ensures termination with the exact successor, but the gap may be large. Popcount may be computed by scanning the W bits.
“Return x + (x AND (-x modulo 2^W)).”: This moves the boundary but loses lower ones. For W=4, x=7, it returns 8, which has one set bit instead of three.

“Move only the lowest set bit to the first zero above it, leaving every other bit unchanged.”: For W=4, x=7, this yields 14, while the smaller valid successor is 11; displaced lower ones must be repacked.

feedback.reason: A fixed sequence of word operations replaces scanning combinations.
details: The method performs a fixed number of operations on words regardless of W. c is nonzero since x>0, and the successor guarantee prevents overflow in r. There is no array, copy or recursion.
